scope: Complete internal owned event capture and JSONL encoding, before future runtime/output admission. Controlled metadata/clock; .NET exception tags are C# bindings, not future-language obligations.
executionStrategy: All 23 cases and actual wire schema checks execute directly; three exact-runtime children retain Information transport, delayed context lifetime and bounded aggregate output. Historical receipts retain their original scope.
authority: Original criteria preserved below; direct user configurable-entry-cap/truncation and creator-disposes decisions take precedence.

criteria.sourceDescription: All required identity fields and every available allowlisted resource field appear; optional unavailable values are omitted and explicit attribute null remains JSON null.
criteria.appliedMeaning: Every required and available allowlisted field, explicit attribute null, absent optional fields, all severity and environment-kind mappings are checked on actual encoded records.

criteria.sourceDescription: Captured trace IDs have 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters and span IDs have 16, neither all zero; later Activity or scope changes cannot change queued evidence.
criteria.appliedMeaning: Real current W3C IDs are sampled before capture; owned facts encode after creator scope/activity disposal and caller changes. Children inherit trace with new spans; barrier-driven workers/stores retain isolated operations and restore their own contexts.

criteria.sourceDescription: Explicit attributes and nonblank event OperationId win the documented scope precedence, while reserved identity/correlation stays unchanged.
criteria.appliedMeaning: Whole event attribute winners remain nested; event IDs override nonblank scopes, blank event IDs fall back. Protected identity/correlation is separately encoded.

criteria.sourceDescription: Timestamp and numeric/string types match the shared schema; record size is checked after escaping, and an oversized event is rejected globally before any output admission.
criteria.appliedMeaning: User truncation amendment replaces ordinary oversize rejection. Actual escaping and LF are measured at three configured caps; encoded producer records also pass the independent development schema/semantic validator. No output admission is implemented.

criteria.sourceDescription: Messages/templates retain supplied text within their limits, ordinary oversized input is rejected, and only the documented exception projection may clip content.
criteria.appliedMeaning: User truncation amendment replaces ordinary oversize rejection. Exact supplied text survives fitting records. Byte fitting marks ordinary loss and exception-local child omissions without mutating facts; a later fitting exception sibling remains. Prior T01/T04 tests continue to verify scalar bounds, invalid data and protected-envelope failure.

existingControls.scope: Malformed native inputs remain invalid; field bounds qualified by the existing full suite.
A protected envelope that cannot fit fails specifically; ordinary payload truncates.
C#-only fault injection of invalid current IDs; no portable reflection requirement.

limits: No CoreLogger/output/worker/provider or admission counters. Holding captured facts across a signal is a capture ownership probe, not delivery evidence.
Native Ubuntu uses the same managed bytes with the actual runtime; full Linux SDK/macOS/release six-family qualification remains pending.
C# runtime exception type/stack and invalid UTF-16 controls are declared native bindings. Cooperative callbacks and prohibited inherited-scope handle misuse retain their documented boundaries.
comparatorControls: native Python corrupted-null control; each final native run requires actual rejection
